page.layout: Running head at top: "NOTÆ." with page number 228 at the top left. Two columns of running text, the left column being a short column of Arabic text and marginal Arabic at the far left margin; the main text column is at the right. Below the main text block there is a short marginal note-free line at the foot. The Arabic column at left is a margin of notes (side="left").

main_text.p: plaraque accepta sunt à Judæis, quibus * nativum est, inquit, Deum hominibus assimilare, adeo ut ipsum usque ad oculorum dolorem ob Noachi diluvium plorantem describant. Certè Judæos & Mohammedi, & ipsius affectus satis illusisse atque in multis impososuisse, nullus dubito, multa autem apud ipsos hujusmodi dicta reperiuntur, qualia & illud in Talmud.Berac. c. 1. Deum singulis noctis vigiliis instar Leonis rugientem dicere אוי שׁרבתי את בית &c. Hei, quòd domum meam devastaverim, & templum meum flammis tradiderim, & filios meos inter gentes in exilium miserim &c. & certè eos nimis ad assimilationem hanc (quam vocant) proclives fuisse, inde patet quod tam sollicitus sit Maimonides in ea è vulgi animis eradicanda, ut librum Moreh aliáque ejus scripta infpicienti, videre est. Hæc Assimilatorum deliria. At cautiores fuerunt alii in his explicandis quæ in Deo Corporeitatem, vel similitudinem cum rebus creatis adstruere viderentur. Ahmed Ebn Hanbali, & David Asphahanienfis, aliíque non pauci Maleci, cujus antea meminimus, sententiam secuti dixerunt

دومن بما ورد فى الكتاب ولا تعرض للتاويل بعد ان نعلم قطعا ان الله عز وجل لا يشبه شيا من المخلوقات وان كل ما تمثل في الوهم فاذا خالفه ومقدره وكانوا يحترزون عن التشبيه الى غاية قالوا من حرك يده عند اقرا قوله خلق بيدي اشار باصبعه عند روايته قلب المومن بين اصبعين من اصابع الرحمن وجب قطع اصبعه i. e. page.notes: Arabic text in the right column is printed in Arabic script; transcribed as printed where legible. Marginal Arabic label "التشبيه–ه / فيهم طباع" at the left margin, and the Hebrew phrase is approximate. Catchword and foot line are uncertain: the word at the foot of the right column reads "ment." as the continuation of "Credi-". The Arabic lines are partly illegible at this scan resolution and may contain errors; the Hebrew phrase is uncertain [?]. Page is from a 17th-century Latin work with Arabic and Hebrew quotations, with a printer's watermark-like mark "Google" in the lower right corner, which is not printed text and is omitted.
